text_post: Age of consent is an artificial construct created to bridge the gap between letting consenting partners do what they want and preventing adults from exploiting children.  In Canada (Or at least Quebec), it was 14 when I was growing up.  Now I think it's back up to 18.  It's been higher than 18 and lower than 14 in different places and at different times.   Like any age limit law (say drinking, voting, or driving), it restricts the underage who are ready and willing, but protects the underaged who are not.  It rightfully punishes adult exploiters of children (usually... unless the predator is female), and unfairly punishes adults with willing underaged partners.  And in some cases punishes underaged males who have sex with underaged females, which is ridiculous. On the whole, I think age of consent laws do more good than harm as long as they are applied to both sexes equally (same conviction rate, same sentence length).  Not to mention the obscenity that a statutory rape victim is often forced to pay child support when he turns 18.  From the examples we see almost every day, we are far from equality there.  A minimum age difference (say 5 years) would also avoid all the messy 17 year old + 18 year old situations.
